correctness.rationale: If x and y original vertices on the two sides are omitted, all xy intervening subdividers are forced; for x,y≥1 every dominating set has at least p+q−1+(x−1)(y−1) vertices. If x=0 or y=0 the size is at least p+q. Thus equality at p+q−1 requires x=1 or y=1 and exactly forced subdividers. Semitotal distinct distance≤2 witnesses exclude one omitted original on each side (the isolated forced subdivider lacks witness) and omitting all opposite-side originals (selected originals then lack witness). Surviving 2≤y≤q−1 and symmetric cases are disjoint and automatically independent. Binomial enumeration gives full polynomial and cardinality; p=q=2 is C8, whose length-8 four-selected-vertex cyclic gaps among (2,2,2,2), permutations (3,2,2,1), and alternating (3,1,3,1) yield 30 sets, exactly 2 independent. Independently enumerated every vertex subset for (p,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4), matching optimizer counts 30,6,20,18,42. The proof covers all p,q≥2; tests only small cases.

value.rationale: Complete classification of *all* minimum semitotal dominating sets and occupancy-polynomial multiplicities for full subdivisions of a fundamental graph family.
